sections.title: Sound of ye
paragraphs: The letter is called (ye) /ˈje/. It usually sounds like the start of (yo) /ˈɟʝo/, which means I. It makes three sounds.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: First, raise the middle of your tongue close to the roof of your mouth. Let voiced air squeeze through smoothly. For the second sound, touch the roof briefly with your tongue, then release the air. For the last sound, keep your tongue high and front like a close vowel. Touch your throat to feel the voice buzz.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: Between vowels, it makes a friction sound as in (mayo) /ˈma.ʝo/. At the start of a word or after n or l, it starts with a firm touch as in (cónyuge) /ˈkon.ɟʝu.xe/. At the end of a word, it sounds like an English ee in (rey) /rei̯/. On its own, the word (y) /i/ makes that same vowel sound.

sections.title: Common pitfalls
paragraphs: Do not make this letter like the English j in jam. That sound pushes the tongue tip forward too much. Keep the tongue tip low behind your bottom teeth. Also, do not pronounce it as a plain English y in yes every time. Give it more friction and buzz.
